case_studies.recommended_db: SQLite (WAL Mode) for local/single-node or PostgreSQL
case_studies.title: Personal Task Management API

case_studies.rationale: Identity requires durable ACID storage for user accounts, RBAC roles, and refresh-token rotation families (PostgreSQL), paired with sub-millisecond brute-force rate limiting in Redis.
case_studies.recommended_db: PostgreSQL (Credentials & Refresh Families) + Redis (Revocation Deny-List & Login Rate Limit)
case_studies.title: Authentication & Authorization Service (OAuth2 + Argon2id + Refresh Rotation)

case_studies.architecture_style: Read-Heavy Cache-Aside + Async Buffered Analytics Pipeline
case_studies.rationale: Read-to-write ratio is 100:1. Redirects (`GET /{code}`) must respond in <2ms via Redis + Go `singleflight` without blocking on synchronous analytics `INSERT`s.
case_studies.recommended_db: PostgreSQL (Base62 Mapping) + Redis (Hot Redirect Cache) + ClickHouse/Timescale (Click Events)
case_studies.title: High-Throughput URL Shortener & Click Analytics

case_studies.architecture_style: Modular Monolith with PostgreSQL FTS (`tsvector` + GIN)
case_studies.rationale: Instead of operating a separate Elasticsearch cluster for <10M articles, PostgreSQL's built-in `tsvector` + `GIN` index provides stemmed full-text search, ranking (`ts_rank_cd`), and ACID publishing workflows in one database.
case_studies.title: Blog & Content Management Backend with Full-Text Search

case_studies.rationale: Checkout spans inventory reservation, coupon validation, payment intent creation, and order confirmation. Modular Monolith + Outbox guarantees atomic order creation and reliable downstream fulfillment events.
case_studies.title: E-Commerce Checkout & Order Orchestration Backend

case_studies.architecture_style: CQRS + Optimistic/Atomic SQL Locking + Temporary Reservation TTL
case_studies.rationale: During a flash sale (50,000 users trying to buy 100 items in 2 seconds), Redis Lua `DECR` acts as an ultra-fast pre-filter so only 100 requests hit PostgreSQL's transactional reservation table.
case_studies.recommended_db: PostgreSQL (Source of Truth) + Redis (Flash-Sale Atomic Pre-Gate)
case_studies.title: High-Concurrency Flash-Sale Inventory Management System

case_studies.architecture_style: Stateful WebSocket Hub per Node + Redis Pub/Sub / NATS Backplane
case_studies.rationale: User A may be connected via WebSocket to Go Pod 1 while User B is connected to Go Pod 2. A Redis Pub/Sub or NATS backplane routes messages between pods, while time-ordered clustering keys store chat history.
case_studies.recommended_db: ScyllaDB / Cassandra or PostgreSQL Partitioned Tables (Messages) + Redis (Presence & Pub/Sub)
case_studies.title: Real-Time WebSocket Chat & Presence Backend

case_studies.architecture_style: Control-Plane Metadata API + Direct-to-S3/MinIO Pre-Signed Uploads
case_studies.rationale: Proxying 2GB video uploads through Go API memory wastes bandwidth and RAM. The Go API issues short-lived S3 pre-signed `PUT` URLs with strict `Content-Length` and SHA-256 checksum constraints, or streams via `io.Reader` magic-byte sniffing.
case_studies.recommended_db: PostgreSQL (File Metadata, Checksums & ACLs) + S3/MinIO Object Storage
case_studies.title: Secure Object & File Storage Service (Pre-Signed URLs & Streaming)

case_studies.architecture_style: Event-Driven Worker Pool + Per-Provider Circuit Breakers + Exponential Backoff & DLQ
case_studies.rationale: External SMS/Email providers (Twilio, SES, FCM) suffer intermittent latency and rate limits. Decoupling dispatch via queues with per-provider circuit breakers and dead-letter queues prevents provider outages from impacting core user APIs.
case_studies.recommended_db: PostgreSQL (Delivery Log & Templates) + RabbitMQ / Kafka (Dispatch Queues)
case_studies.title: Multi-Channel Notification Delivery Service (Email, SMS, Push, Webhook)

case_studies.rationale: Application-level overlap checks (`SELECT count(*) WHERE start < $end AND end > $start`) fail under `READ COMMITTED` when two users book overlapping time ranges simultaneously. PostgreSQL's `EXCLUDE USING gist (room_id WITH =, tstzrange(check_in, check_out) WITH &&)` enforces non-overlapping intervals at the storage index level!
case_studies.title: Hotel / Flight / Clinic Booking & Time-Slot Reservation System

case_studies.architecture_style: Two-Phase Authorize/Capture State Machine + Immutable Double-Entry Ledger
case_studies.rationale: Payments never overwrite a single float column. Every movement of funds (Authorization Hold -> Capture -> Platform Fee -> Merchant Payout -> Refund) is recorded as balanced debit/credit rows summing to zero (`SUM(amount_cents) = 0`).
case_studies.title: Payment Processing Gateway & Double-Entry Settlement Engine

case_studies.architecture_style: Shared-Schema Multi-Tenancy with PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) + Tenant Context Middleware
case_studies.rationale: In B2B SaaS, forgetting `WHERE tenant_id = $1` on a single query leaks Customer A's data to Customer B. Enabling PostgreSQL RLS (`USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid)`) enforces tenant isolation at the database engine level as a defense-in-depth safety net.
case_studies.title: Multi-Tenant B2B SaaS Backend with Row-Level Security (RLS)

case_studies.architecture_style: Saga Pattern with Compensating Transactions + Transactional Outbox + Kafka
case_studies.rationale: When Order Service, Payment Service, and Warehouse Service own separate databases, distributed 2-Phase Commit (XA) destroys availability. A Saga coordinates local ACID transactions via Kafka events and executes explicit compensating actions (`RefundPayment`, `ReleaseStock`) if a downstream step fails.
case_studies.recommended_db: PostgreSQL per Microservice + Apache Kafka Event Backbone
case_studies.title: Event-Driven Distributed Order Processing System (Saga Orchestrator)

case_studies.architecture_style: Multi-Tier Caching (In-Process L1 LRU + Redis L2 + Singleflight) + Zero-Alloc Hot Paths + Read Replicas
case_studies.rationale: At 50,000+ RPS, even Redis network roundtrips add up. Combining a short-TTL (2s) in-process sharded L1 cache, a 60s Redis L2 cache guarded by `singleflight`, `pgx/v5` binary protocol, and `GOMEMLIMIT` tuning achieves sub-2ms p99 latency.
case_studies.recommended_db: PostgreSQL Primary + Read Replicas + Redis Cluster + Go In-Memory L1 Cache
case_studies.title: High-Traffic Low-Latency Public API Service (50,000+ RPS Architecture)

case_study_steps.content_text: Single static Go binary + Litestream continuous WAL backup to S3, or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL.

case_study_steps.title: 3. Non-Functional Requirements

case_study_steps.content_text: Multi-Tier Caching (In-Process L1 LRU + Redis L2 + Singleflight) + Zero-Alloc Hot Paths + Read Replicas — At 50,000+ RPS, even Redis network roundtrips add up. Combining a short-TTL (2s) in-process sharded L1 cache, a 60s Redis L2 cache guarded by `singleflight`, `pgx/v5` binary protocol, and `GOMEMLIMIT` tuning achieves sub-2ms p99 latency.

case_study_steps.title: 9. Testing Strategy

case_study_steps.content_text: Enforce object-level ownership (`WHERE id = $1 AND user_id/tenant_id = $2` — OWASP API1:2023 BOLA), bound payload size via `http.MaxBytesReader` (OWASP API4:2023), use parameterized SQL queries exclusively, and validate outbound URLs in `net.Dialer.Control` (OWASP API7:2023 SSRF).
case_study_steps.title: 10. Security Considerations

case_study_steps.content_text: Cover hot read paths with composite B-Tree/GIN indexes verified via `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`; replace deep `OFFSET` with keyset cursor pagination; bound `*sql.DB` / `pgxpool` connection limits (`MaxOpenConns`, `MaxIdleConns`).

case_study_steps.title: 12. Deployment Strategy

case_study_steps.content_text: Allowing unbounded request queueing during downstream slowdowns instead of bounded concurrency load shedding; leaving `net/http/pprof` exposed on the public internet port instead of an internal admin port.
case_study_steps.title: 13. Common Engineering Mistakes

case_study_steps.content_text: Can start as an internal module inside a Modular Monolith using SQLite WAL (single-node) or PostgreSQL (multi-replica), and only extract into an independent gRPC/Kafka service if organizational boundaries or asymmetric scaling (>10,000 RPS) justify the operational overhead.
